record.paper_title: Some open problems on excluding a uniform matroid
record.context_brief: Efficient computation of flat-cover number tau_t
record.original_question: For a fixed integer t > 1, can one efficiently compute tau_t(M), the minimum number of rank-t flats needed to cover all elements of a matroid M?

evidence.quote: For a matroid M and integer t we let τt(M) denote the minimum number of rank-t flats that are required to cover all elements of M. Thus τ1(M) is the number of points (rank-one flats) in M. (For fixed t > 1, can we compute τt(M) efficiently?)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a matroid on a finite ground set $E(M)$, with rank function $r$ and closure operator $\mathrm{cl}$. A flat of $M$ is a subset $F \subseteq E(M)$ with $\mathrm{cl}(F) = F$, and a rank-$t$ flat is a flat $F$ with $r(F) = t$. For a positive integer $t$, define
$$\tau_t(M) = \min\{\,|\mathcal{F}| : \mathcal{F} \text{ is a collection of rank-}t\text{ flats of } M \text{ with } \bigcup_{F\in\mathcal{F}} F = E(M)\,\},$$
the minimum number of rank-$t$ flats needed to cover every element of $M$ (so $\tau_1(M)$ is the number of points of $M$).

Fix an integer $t > 1$. Does there exist an algorithm that, given a matroid $M$ (accessed via a rank or independence oracle, or specified by a representation over a field), computes $\tau_t(M)$ in time polynomial in $|E(M)|$?
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not return any direct results addressing the efficient computability of the flat-cover number $\tau_t(M)$ for fixed $t > 1$. No paper appears to claim a polynomial-time algorithm nor a hardness result for this specific quantity, so the status remains unverified.
